factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Configure Startup applications in Windows
factual_notes.note: Registered startup applications can be configured from Settings or Task Manager; Task Manager adds impact details. Startup folders cover some apps not registered with a startup task. Microsoft warns that registry modifications can have unintended consequences.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Configure Startup applications in Windows
factual_notes.note: Settings uses On to start an app automatically at sign-in and Off to prevent automatic start. Task Manager uses Enable and Disable for the same registered list.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Configure Startup applications in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft defines High impact as more than one second of CPU time or more than 3 MB of disk usage; Not Measured means the enabled app has insufficient measurement data; None indicates disabled.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Tips to improve PC performance in Windows
factual_notes.note: Apps that run at startup can slow boot and increase background usage; Microsoft recommends disabling apps that are not needed automatically and reviewing Startup apps in Task Manager.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Windows: Take control of your Windows startup
factual_notes.note: Too many automatic apps can slow startup and continue using battery or performance resources, but frequently used apps may be convenient to keep enabled.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Desktop Startup apps compatibility guidance
factual_notes.note: Microsoft's developer guidance treats startup impact and unnecessary duplicate functionality as design considerations; this supports selective review rather than disabling everything.
The April 2026 message center noted improved performance for launching apps listed under Settings > Apps > Startup. It did not describe a broad issue blocking normal startup toggles.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Windows 11 version 24H2 release health
factual_notes.note: The current 24H2 health page was checked for version-specific context; no broad startup-app toggle failure was identified in the opened current known-issues summary.

topic_context.difference_from_existing: This how-to is limited to choosing, disabling, testing, and re-enabling individual sign-in apps without uninstalling them; the existing startup-performance article diagnoses slow boot impact rather than teaching this controlled settings task.
